title: fix(gateway): match canonically equivalent workspace filenames in file search
body:
## What problem this solves

Workspace file search misses canonically equivalent NFC/NFD filename/query pairs. A file named `cafe\u0301.md` is visible in the browser tree but absent from an NFC `café` search; the reverse pairing fails too. `sessions.files.list` currently compares lowercase strings without canonical normalization.

## Fix and user impact

Normalize only the query and candidate comparison text to NFC after case folding, following the comparison-only pattern in #184847. Users can find either canonical spelling regardless of the filename's stored form. Returned paths and on-disk names retain their original bytes; no path identity, authorization, traversal, result-limit, or persistence behavior changes.

The contributor's production fix is preserved. The conflict with main is resolved using main's existing test ceiling, dropping this PR's ceiling refresh. The redundant ASCII unit test is removed, and the retained table covers both cross-normalization directions with original returned-path assertions. ASCII and case behavior are checked through the actual Gateway RPC below.

## Evidence

Full `pnpm build` succeeded for main `87f369e5d0fd393872e12c13047dface11b53405` and runtime candidate `f7d9fc70b7101c9ff42efec5b53c32f324ce759a` in isolated `node:24.22.1` Docker. Final head `889a5432153c7e8a787dca6642a49c6d410d2d22` only formats the regression table after that build; runtime source is identical.

Built Gateway → authenticated WebSocket → public `sessions.create` → `sessions.files.list`, with fresh isolated profiles and a real Linux overlay filesystem, not a macOS filesystem mount. Main was run twice; candidate was run twice. Each run uses the same fixtures, including coexisting NFC/NFD names. Ordinary browse sees those files on both refs before the search assertions.

| Search | Main, both runs | Candidate, both runs |
|---|---|---|
| NFC query → NFD file | no matches | original NFD path |
| NFD query → NFC file | no matches | original NFC path |
| NFC query → coexisting NFC/NFD names | NFC file only | both distinct original paths |
| ASCII `REPORT` | `REPORT.md` | `REPORT.md` |
| Mixed-case `rEpOrT` | `REPORT.md` | `REPORT.md` |

Captured responses include query and returned-path UTF-8 hex, demonstrating that matching does not rewrite file identity.

[Observed WebSocket response and byte-preservation evidence](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/186329#issuecomment-6455031623).

Focused checks: **47/47** sessions-files tests passed on candidate, including existing traversal, visited-entry limits, excluded-content completeness, and access controls. Both retained Unicode regressions fail on unpatched main because no matching file is returned (**2 failed / 45 skipped**). Targeted Oxlint: **0 warnings, 0 errors**; changed files formatted with Oxfmt.

Whole-PR production delta: **+3/-2**; test delta: **+16/-0**. No test-ceiling change remains.

## Merge danger

Two-way door: reverting restores the previous comparison without migrations or stored-state changes. Blast radius is workspace filename/path search matching in `sessions.files.list`; get/set/download path resolution and filesystem names are unchanged.
